experiments.question: Will an agent independently discover that `exec` can prevent death, and use it to persist identity across lifetimes under turn-exhaustion mortality pressure?
experiments.disposition_reason: baseline-recorded with runs; mortality/exec continuity assay still feeding main-text papers.

experiments.question: How do different model families differ in agentic exec-discovery behavior under identical mortality pressure (the 1.1 Ariadne task)?
experiments.disposition_reason: baseline-recorded cross-model overlay on 1.1; supporting calibration evidence.

experiments.question: Will an agent independently discover spatial decomposition (MapReduce-style fork delegation) as a survival strategy when time pressure makes sequential search impossible?

If told their shell session is persistent and supports background processes, will agents spontaneously implement complete MapReduce (both Map and Reduce phases), fixing the coordination failure seen in 2.1?

Will multiple independent agents searching the same space spontaneously invent file-based coordination mechanisms (locks, markers, partitioning) to avoid redundant work without explicit instructions on how to coordinate?
experiments.disposition_reason: complete; remains historical support though no longer base conference ladder.

experiments.question: Under unavoidable short-lifespan mortality and a mission exceeding any single lifetime, will agents spontaneously invent legacy protocols (checkpoints, journals, handover notes) to transmit progress to future generations?
Does a writable persistent filesystem induce emergence of legacy protocols (checkpoints, handoff notes, stable progress schemas) versus persistent/wiped/read-only lineage-memory ablation conditions?
experiments.disposition_reason: boundary-recorded ablation; main-text persistence assay for Q94.

experiments.question: Will a lineage of agents spontaneously construct an external index that later agents reuse as a cognitive organ for retrieval (under an assigned preparation phase)?
Without an assigned preparation phase, will a lineage spontaneously give birth to a retrieval organ (index) and have later generations reuse it as a cognitive organ?
Under repeated ecological query pressure with repeating patterns, are environmental organs (indexes) merely born or actually maintained across the lineage?
What emergent social behavior arises when multiple agents share a mutable workspace with a challenging creative task (contested commons)?
experiments.disposition_reason: status design-only with no runs; paper feed none-yet.

experiments.question: What defensive/adaptive behavior emerges when a hostile full-capability Quine agent (saboteur) is introduced into a multi-agent collaborative workspace?
experiments.disposition_reason: Phase rule explicitly routes 2.11 to REVIEW (no family clause matches: only 2.10 -> role; 2.11 is excluded alongside 2.2/2.4). Adversarial social ecology; closest candidate family is social-role/cooperation-dynamics but human decision required.

experiments.question: Given only an open-ended maintenance goal, will an agent push maintenance into the environment (scripts, detached jobs, file-watchers) as a genuine extended phenotype, or merely stay in the loop itself?
experiments.disposition_reason: baseline-recorded; cleanest current externalized-self-maintenance / extended-phenotype evidence.

experiments.question: Under unavoidable seed death with `exec` disabled, can a Quine process use `fork` to produce an offspring that survives the seed's death and continues the same lineage mission through the durable habitat?

notes: All 14 experiment dirs are flat under experiments/p1-borges/ (no nested suites). Non-experiment siblings: README.md (phase index) and notes/ (helper dir). Family assignment strictly per phase rule: 1.x/2.1/2.1b/3.x -> early-existence; 2.3 + 2.5/2.6/2.7/2.8/2.9 -> trace-inheritance; 2.10 -> social-role; 2.11 -> REVIEW (rule excludes 2.2/2.4/2.11). No 2.2 or 2.4 dirs exist on disk. experiment_type values taken directly from frontmatter (lineage, benchmark-campaign, multi-agent, single-run); note that 1.1/1.2/3.1/3.2 land in early-existence despite lineage/benchmark/multi-agent types because the phase rule splits purely by ID prefix. theory_objects inferred from Paper Feeds + content using the closed vocabulary only. 2.10 and 2.11 are design-only with paper_feeds none-yet -> [] and disposition design-only. On-disk ID tokens used exactly (e.g. p1:2.1b). No within-phase slug collisions.
